title: A supply shock

controls.label: SRAS shift (billions at every price level)

predict.q: The economy starts in long-run equilibrium. The world price of oil doubles and SRAS shifts left. What happens in the short run?

options.s: Price level rises, real output rises
options.fb: That is the effect of a rise in AD. Higher costs shift SRAS left, which moves the economy up along AD: higher prices, less output.

options.s: Price level rises, real output falls
options.fb: Stagflation: SRAS −125 gives price level 115 and output 1,950, a gap of −2.5%.

options.s: Price level rises, real output unchanged
options.fb: Output is fixed only on a vertical curve. Here the economy moves up along a downward-sloping AD, so less real output is bought.

task: Move the SRAS slider left, then right, and watch the price level, real output and unemployment.

target.do: Move the SRAS slider to the left, then press Check.

takeaway: A negative supply shock brings stagflation: higher prices and lower output at the same time.
